source.title: Exploring the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Beyond In-Distribution Data

record.file_problem: The post text is present, but it refers to plots that are not included. No numerical results are given.
record.tranche_reason: The post explicitly says it replicates the PRH analysis on a new dataset, ImageNet-O, and also measures alignment-score correlations on random images. The text does not provide enough methodological detail to verify the exact recipe.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes for alignment-score correlations on ImageNet-O and random images. It does not name the models or specify the correlation measure, its numerical values, or how the random images were generated. The linked notebook was not examined. The in-distribution results are described as the original paper's results, not reported here as new measurements.
record.test_reason: The post reruns the PRH alignment analysis, apparently with the same code base (a fork of platonic-rep), on ImageNet-O and on random images. Its own results bear on whether measured convergence depends on the input data (V6). The post gives no numbers, no model list and no measure details, and the plots are missing, so the evidence is only the author's qualitative statements.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The author concludes that PRH alignment correlations hold on OOD data (ImageNet-O) but are much lower on random images. He takes this as evidence that the convergence reflects shared structure rather than training-distribution overlap or spurious high-capacity agreement. His claim is hedged ('highly likely that there could be').
record.recipe_differences: The post describes a replication of the PRH analysis using ImageNet-O and random images. It does not state enough methodological detail to verify that the original measurement was reproduced exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Input dataset: correlations are described as strong on ImageNet-O and much lower on random images.
record.problems: The post provides no numerical correlations, named model list, detailed measurement procedure, uncertainty estimates, or included plots. The method cannot be checked from the supplied text alone.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported in-distribution row was added because the text attributes those results to the original paper rather than reporting them as this post's own measurements.

untested.parts: The post says it re-evaluates 'correlations between alignment scores', which may be PRH's alignment-versus-competence analysis. It does not say this, and no size or capability trend is described, so V1 cannot be assessed from the text.
No mapping, stitching or interchangeability tests.
Similarity metric and its settings (e.g. number of neighbours) are not varied. Only the input data is varied.

The post argues against the training-data-overlap explanation. But the models are still trained on shared ImageNet data, and only the evaluation inputs are out of distribution, so shared training data as a cause is not actually tested. Incompleteness or plateau of alignment is not examined.

missing.what: Plots comparing in-distribution and ImageNet-O alignment correlations, and the random-image plot. Also which correlation is computed: possibly alignment versus model competence, which would bear on V1.
missing.locator: Post body, referenced plots (not in text); linked notebook OOD-experiments.ipynb

record.verdict_notes: This is a short LessWrong post with no numbers, unnamed models, and missing plots; a commenter asks how the correlations were computed. The ImageNet-O result is evaluation-OOD only, since the models share ImageNet training. The author's anti-data-overlap reading therefore does not test V7's shared-training-data cause. The record's V6 limits_scope label for r1 is changed to challenges, based on the explicit 'persist' statement, with low weight given the missing values.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep is reported.
No vision-language or paired image-caption comparison is reported.
No comparison across random initializations or shared features/subspaces is reported.
No mapping, stitching, or other representation interchangeability test is reported.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are tested.
The post compares natural-image and random-image inputs, but gives no numerical effect sizes or details about alternative similarity measures or settings.
The post does not test whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or establish what causes the reported alignment.
